  2. Creating Strong Everyday Account Habits Good account management is primarily about consistency. Use a Unique Password A strong password should be unique to the edu email account. Using the same password for several services creates unnecessary problems because one compromised service can affect other accounts. A better approach is to use a different password for important accounts. A password manager can help users create and store unique passwords without requiring them to memorize every password individually. Make Passwords Long and Memorable Long passwords or passphrases are generally easier to manage when they combine several unrelated words with appropriate numbers or symbols. For example, a person might create a memorable phrase and transform it into a unique passphrase according to the requirements of their institution. Avoid using easily guessed information such as: ● Birth dates ● School names ● Favorite sports teams ● Simple number sequences ● Names of relatives ● Common phrases The goal is to create a password that is difficult for another person to guess while remaining manageable for the account owner. Use Multi-Factor Authentication When Available Many educational institutions provide multi-factor authentication. This adds another verification step when signing in. Depending on the institution, authentication may involve: ● An authenticator application ● A verification code ● A security key ● A registered device ● Another approved verification method Students should follow their institution's official setup instructions. Multi-factor authentication also teaches an important digital-literacy concept: account access does not have to depend on a password alone. Keep Recovery Information Current Account recovery information can become especially important when a person forgets a password or changes devices. If the institution permits recovery information to be updated, users should ensure that the information is accurate. They should also understand the difference between official recovery procedures and unsolicited messages claiming to provide account recovery assistance. The safest starting point is normally the institution's official IT support page or help desk.

  3. Recognizing Suspicious Messages and Learning Email Awareness Email literacy is an important educational skill because inboxes can contain many different types of communication. Students should learn how to examine messages carefully instead of automatically clicking every link or opening every attachment. Check the Sender Look closely at the sender's address. An unfamiliar or unusual address deserves additional attention, particularly if the message claims to represent: ● The school ● An instructor ● A financial office ● A technology department ● A scholarship organization ● A government agency A display name can sometimes look familiar while the actual email address is different. Examine Links Before Opening Them When an email contains a link, consider whether the destination makes sense. On many devices, hovering over a link can reveal its destination. A student can ask: ● Does the address belong to the expected institution? ● Does the domain look correct? ● Is the message asking for information that normally would not be requested by email? ● Does the link lead somewhere unrelated to the stated purpose? When uncertain, users can navigate to the institution's website directly instead of following the email link. Be Careful With Attachments Attachments can be useful for education, but they should be opened thoughtfully. Common academic attachments include: ● Course documents ● Reading materials ● Forms ● Research papers ● Schedules ● Presentation files Before opening an unexpected attachment, confirm that it was actually expected. If a message appears unusual, contacting the supposed sender through a known communication method can provide clarification. Understand Urgency Tactics Some unwanted messages attempt to make people act immediately. Examples might include statements such as: ● "Your account will be closed today." ● "Immediate verification required." ● "You have only a few minutes." ● "Your payment information must be updated." Educational email literacy means slowing down and evaluating the message. A short pause can make it easier to identify inconsistencies. Learn From Suspicious Messages Instead of simply deleting suspicious emails, students can use them as learning opportunities. They can examine: ● The sender address ● The writing style ● The request being made ● The link destination ● The attachment type ● The sense of urgency ● The information being requested This develops practical digital-literacy skills that extend beyond academic email.

Instead of manually scrolling through hundreds of messages, students can search using: ● Sender names ● Course titles ● Subject keywords ● Dates ● File names ● Specific phrases Learning effective email search techniques is a valuable productivity skill. Use Calendar Integration Some academic email systems connect with calendars. Students can use calendar features to organize: ● Assignment deadlines ● Examination dates ● Office hours ● Group meetings ● Research appointments ● Academic events This can help transform email information into actionable schedules. Separate Important Messages Students can identify messages that need future attention. For example, an email containing an important registration deadline can be marked or organized so that it is easier to find later. The purpose is not to keep every message forever. Instead, students should develop a system for identifying information that has continuing academic value. Clean the Inbox Regularly A clean inbox can reduce distractions.   9. Saving important documents appropriately.

For academic communication, it is often enough to provide the information required to solve the specific problem. Verify Recipients Before sending an email, check the recipient address carefully. This is especially important when sending: ● Assignments ● Research documents ● Academic records ● Group-project materials ● Personal information Auto-complete features can sometimes select a different recipient with a similar name. Taking a few seconds to verify the address can prevent an accidental disclosure. Use Institutional Channels Appropriately Schools often provide different systems for different types of information. Students should follow institutional instructions regarding where specific information should be submitted. Step 6: Establish a Daily Email Routine Set aside a specific period for checking academic email. For many students, checking once in the morning and once later in the day may be sufficient, depending on academic requirements. The important point is consistency. Step 7: Evaluate Messages Carefully Before clicking a link or opening an unexpected attachment, review the sender and message content. When something appears unusual, verify it independently. Step 8: Protect Personal Information Before sending an email, check the recipient and review the contents. Share only information appropriate for the communication. Step 9: Connect Important Information to a Calendar When an email contains a deadline or appointment, transfer it to a calendar or task system. This reduces the chance of forgetting important dates. Step 10: Review the Account Regularly Once a month, review: ● Account settings ● Connected devices ● Authentication methods ● Recovery information ● Inbox organization ● Unnecessary subscriptions Regular reviews make account management a normal part of digital life.

Common Mistakes to Avoid Using One Password Everywhere Different accounts should have different passwords whenever practical. Ignoring Institutional Messages Important academic information can arrive through email, so checking the inbox regularly is useful. item.title: Stanford CS224N - Lecture 4 : Dependency Parsing
item.content:encoded:
The linguistuc structure of sentences - two veiws

자연어 문장은 단순히 단어들이 순서대로 나열된 구조가 아니라 단어들이 하나의 의미있는 구를 이루고, 구들이 모여 더 큰 구를 이루어 문장을 형성한다. 문장을 계층적인 구성성분의 조합으로 바라보는 관점이 Constituency이다.

문장 구조를 바라보는 또 다른 관점은 Dependency structure이다. 이는 각 단어가 어떤 단어를 수식하거나 의존하는 지를 나타낸다. 사람은 언어를 단어의 선형적인 나열로 받아들이지만 실제 의미를 이해하기 위해서는 어떤 단어가 어떤 단어에 연결 되어야 하는지 구조적 관계를 파악해야 한다.

예를 들어 영어에서 가장 모호한 문제를 일으키는 것이 전치사 구인데 위처럼 의존관계가 어디에 연결되느냐에 따라 전치사구의 해석이 모호해진다. 또한 전치사 구가 많아질 수록 가능한 문장구조가 매우 많아진다. 조정 범위 모호성 문제도 존재한다.

Dependency Grammer and Dependency Structure

문장 속 단어들 사이의 관계를 방향 있는 화살표로 연결하면 전체적으로 dependency tree가 된다. head와 의존하는 dependent 사이의 방향 있는 연결로 나타난다.

그런데 실제 NLP 모델에서 활용할 때, 컴퓨터가 이런 것을 배우기 위해서는 정답 구조가 필요하다. 이에 treebank가 구축되어 여러 언어에서 공통된 dependency annotation 체계를 제공하는 UD가 등장한다.

단어와 단어 사이의 dependent를 붙일 때 다음과 같은 4가지를 참고한다. 참고로 마지막 4번은 head가 몇 개, 어떤 종류의 dependent를 요구하거나 허용하는가를 말하는데, "이 단어가 원래 이렇게 많은 dependent를 갖는 게 자연스러운가?"와 같은 것을 판단한다고 볼 수 있다. 위의 비투영종속이란 dependency 관계가 서로 가로질러 화살표가 교차하는 것인데 이 dependency parser를 설계할 때 비투영 종속까지 허용할 것인가? 가 이슈이다.

CFG의 constituency tree에서 각 constituent의 head를 하나씩 선택하여 dependency structure로 변환한 경우에는 projective structure가 만들어진다. 이러면 대부분 projective하다. 하지만 실제로는 의문문이나 특정 어순 변화처럼 의미적으로 연결된 요소가 문장 안에 멀리 떨어져 나타나는 경우는 비투영 종속이 필요할 수 있다.

Methods of Dependency Parsing

Dependency Parsing에는 여러 방식이 있는데 그 중에서 Transition based Parsing이라는 전이기반 구문 분석을 살펴본다.

Greedy transition-based parsing 여기서 핵심은 dependency 트리를 만들 때 parser가 현재 상태를 보고 행동을 하나씩 선택하면서 tree를 만드는 것이다. stack은 현재 처리중인 단어들, buffer는 아직 처리하지 않은 단어 그리고 dependecy arcs A 는 지금까지 만든 의존 관계들을 나타낸다.

이렇게 단어를 분석하기 전에 우선 shift로 buffer를 stack으로 가져오는 과정을 수행한다. 이후 dependency 관계를 확정할 수 있을때 (I ate) Arc를 하는데 위의 예시에서는 왼쪽에 있는 I가 ate에 대한 dependent이므로 Left Arc를 수행한다. 계속 반복하면서 shift 하고 arc를 해서 트리를 만들어 나가는 것이다.

여기서 중요한 점은 위에 예시에서 처음에 우리는 정답을 알고 있기에 shift를 할지 arc를 할지 바로 결정할 수 있었다면 parser는 각 단계에서 하나씩 단계적으로 결정해 나가는 과정을 거친다는 것이다.

그러면 parser는 현재 상태를 보고 스스로 어떻게 결정할 수 있을까?

MaltParser에서는 이를 분류문제라고 한다.

현재 parser 상태가 주어지면 이를 binary indicator feature로 표현한 뒤 다음행동을 예측하는데, 이를 머신러닝 classifier가 수행하는 것이다. 여기서 사람이 기호적인 조건을 정의하고 그 조건이 현재 parser 상태에 성립하는 지를 0/1로 표현한 것이다.

하지만 이렇게 만든 결과가 상당히 부정확하다는 사실을 알 수 있다. 연결 자체를 틀리거나, 관계의 종류를 틀렸다고 볼 수 있다.

그래서 평가는 두 종류인데 여기서 UAS는 올바른 head에 붙였나를 보는 것이고, LAS는 올바른 head와 dependency label까지 맞았는지를 보는 것이다.

그러니까 연결 구조는 꽤 맞추었어도 연결관계를 많이 틀린 것으로 알 수 있다.

또한 이 방식 자체가 projective dependency tree만 만들 수 있어서 실제 정답이 non-projective이면 구조상 정확한 정답을 만들 수 없는 경우가 있다.

Why do we gain from a neural dependency parser? Indicator Features Revisited

아까 봤던 MaltParser와 같은 전통적인 머신러닝 방식의 문제점이다.

위에서 본 것처럼 sparse 문제가 있고, 모든 유용한 패턴을 담기 어려워 일부 기능이 누락될 수 있다(지표 특징 문제). 또한 조합을 많이 계산해야하기 때문에 비용이 많이 든다. Neural Approach 그래서 신경망 기반 전이구분 분석기를 이용하는데 사람이 수많은 이진특징을 직접 만드는 게 아니라 neural network가 밀집되고 압축된 벡터 표현으로 학습하는 것이다.

First win : Distributed Representations

일단 분산 표현을 한다는 측면에서 다르다.

임베딩을 하면 하나의 단어가 이진표현이 아니라 여러 차원의 값에 걸쳐 표현이 된다. 우선 위의 표처럼 parser에서 볼 위치를 정한 뒤 각 위치에서 3가지 정보를 뽑는다. 그런 다음 각 기호를 embedding vetor로 바꾼다. 여기서 하나의 기호를 가지면 embedding table에서 해당 벡터를 찾아오는 것이다. 이제 모든 embedding을 이어붙여 하나의 긴 vector를 만든다. 이는 신경망에게 현재 parser의 상태를 설명해준다. 그러면 이제 이걸 신경망에 넣고 다음 action의 점수를 낸다음 가장 적절한 것을 골라 다음 단계로 진행한다.

Second win : Deep Learning classifiers are non-linear classifiers

그리고 선형 분류기가 아니라 비선형 분류기라는 점에서 다르다. 여러 층과 비선형 활성화 함수를 사용해서 더 복잡한 비선형 결정경계를 학습할 수 있다. 따라서 더 복잡한 패턴과 feature간 상호작용을 학습할 수 있는 것! 아래처럼 다음 trasition의 확률은 소프트맥스로 예측하고, 학습 시 cross-entropy loss를 역전파하여 parameter와 embedding을 함께 업데이트한다.

Graph-based dependency parsers

위의 잠깐 나왔던 depedency parsing의 또다른 방식으로 이것은 앞서 보았던 Transition-based parser처럼 행동을 하나씩 수행하여 트리를 만드는 대신 각 단어가 다른 각 단어를 head로 가질 가능성이 얼마나 좋은가?를 판단하는 것이다.

즉, 여기서 가능한 dependency edge마다 score를 계산하는 것이고 이는 문장의 모든 단어에 대해서 연결에 점수를 주는 것이라 할 수 있다. 그렇게 전체 dependency score의 합이 가장 높은 올바른 트리를 선택하는 것이고, 이때 하나의 정상적인 트리이면서(cycle이 생기지 않으면서) 총점이 최대가 되는 연결 조합을 찾는데 여기서 MST 알고리즘이 사용된다.

MST는 최소신장 트리로 .. 그래프의 모든 정점을 연결하면서 사이클을 만들지 않고 간선 가중치 합이 최소가 되도록 고르는 트리 여기서는 최소냐 최대냐만 바뀌어서 이 알고리즘을 사용한 것이다.

여기에서도 신경망을 붙인다면? 정확도는 향상되었지만, 아쉽게도 여기서는 transition처럼 행동을 순차적으로 몇번 더 고르는 것이 아니라 가능한 dependency를 많이 비교해야 해서 더 느려진다.

Instead, it means understanding which information should be broadly visible and which information should remain limited to selected people. Phone Number Privacy A Telegram account is associated with a phone number, but users can review the platform's available privacy controls for deciding how that number is displayed. This is particularly useful when joining educational groups, professional communities, hobby groups, or large public discussions. People may communicate with others whom they do not personally know, so understanding phone-number visibility can help users make deliberate choices. Profile Photo and Personal Information Profile photos, biographies, usernames, and other profile details can provide useful context to contacts. At the same time, users should think about how much personal information they want to make available. A practical approach is to keep profile information appropriate for the audience. For a professional or educational account, a simple profile and clear username may be sufficient. Users should avoid placing unnecessary personal details in public-facing areas. Last Seen and Online Information Telegram provides controls related to last-seen and online visibility. Learning how these options work can help users manage expectations around availability. For example, a student may not want every group member to know when they are online. A professional may prefer to respond to messages according to a schedule rather than creating an expectation of immediate availability. Understanding these settings supports healthier communication habits. Learning Outcome After studying Telegram privacy settings, a user should be able to explain:
  3. What personal information appears on a Telegram profile.
  4. Which privacy options are available.

  7. Protecting Account Access Through Better Authentication Habits Account access is another important part of learning how to use Telegram safely. Authentication is the process through which a service confirms that a person is authorized to use an account. For everyday users, understanding authentication helps create better habits around verification codes, passwords, devices, and login sessions. Understanding Verification Codes Telegram may use login codes as part of the account sign-in process. Users should understand that these codes are intended for account access and should be treated as private information. A useful digital habit is simple: do not casually share login codes with another person. Messages asking someone to forward a code should be considered carefully because the code is connected to account access. Using Two-Step Verification Telegram provides two-step verification as an additional account-protection feature. Learning how this feature works can give users another layer of control over account access. When setting up an additional password, users should choose something unique and memorable. It is also important to understand any recovery options offered by the platform and keep associated information accurate. Useful habits include: ● Avoiding simple, predictable passwords ● Avoiding the same password across multiple services ● Using a reputable password manager when appropriate ● Keeping recovery information current ● Avoiding passwords based on easily known personal details These practices can be applied to email, social networks, cloud services, educational platforms, and workplace applications. Why Authentication Knowledge Matters Authentication literacy helps people understand that account ownership is connected to more than simply knowing a username. Access may involve a phone number, verification code, password, device session, or recovery method. Learning these relationships allows users to respond more thoughtfully when signing in from a new device or reviewing account activity.
  8. Managing Telegram Groups, Channels, and Communities Telegram is widely used for group communication and channels. These spaces can be valuable for education, hobbies, professional collaboration, community announcements, and public information. Learning how to participate effectively is therefore both a communication skill and a digital citizenship skill. Groups as Learning Environments A Telegram group can function like a digital classroom or discussion room. Members may exchange study materials, ask questions, share reminders, and coordinate projects. Students can use groups to: ● Discuss assignments ● Share study schedules ● Exchange useful resources ● Organize project tasks ● Ask questions ● Coordinate meetings However, productive participation requires communication discipline. Users should read group rules, stay on topic, and avoid sending unnecessary messages. Channels as Information Sources Channels are generally designed for broadcasting information to an audience. They can be useful for announcements, educational updates, news discussions, community information, and specialized interests. Learning to evaluate channel content is an important digital-literacy skill. Users should consider the source, date, context, supporting information, and purpose of a post before treating it as authoritative. Communication Etiquette Good Telegram communication includes: ● Writing clearly ● Respecting different opinions ● Avoiding unnecessary repetition ● Reading previous messages before asking questions ● Keeping sensitive information out of public conversations ● Following community guidelines ● Using direct messages appropriately These habits are transferable to email, workplace chat, online classrooms, and other communication platforms.
  9. Developing Responsible Information-Sharing Skills Telegram makes it easy to send documents, images, videos, links, voice messages, and other information. This convenience makes information-sharing literacy especially important. The key lesson is to pause before sharing. Users should understand what they are sending, who will receive it, and whether the information is appropriate for that audience. Think Before Sharing A useful decision process involves three questions: What am I sharing? Identify whether the material contains personal, educational, professional, financial, or private information. Who will receive it? A message sent to one trusted contact is different from a message posted in a large group or public channel. Why am I sharing it? Having a clear purpose helps users avoid unnecessary disclosure. Managing Shared Files Telegram can be useful for transferring documents between devices. Students might send notes, while professionals may exchange work materials. Good file-management habits include: ● Checking file names before sending ● Removing unnecessary personal information ● Confirming the intended recipient ● Organizing downloaded documents ● Deleting outdated copies when appropriate ● Avoiding accidental sharing in large groups These are useful skills for digital organization generally. Recognizing Unclear Information Online messages can contain incomplete or misleading information. Learning to verify important claims is part of responsible digital citizenship. Before forwarding information, users can ask: ● Who originally created it? ● Is the information current? ● Is there supporting evidence? ● Is the message presented without context? ● Can the claim be confirmed through a reliable source? This habit helps users become more careful consumers of digital information.
  10. Building Healthy and Productive Telegram Usage Habits Using Telegram safely is also connected to time management, attention management, and communication balance.Messaging applications can become part of everyday routines. Without clear habits, frequent notifications and group activity may interrupt study, work, rest, or family time. Managing Notifications Telegram offers notification controls that can help users organize their attention. For example, users may choose to: ● Mute nonessential groups ● Keep important conversations visible ● Adjust notification sounds ● Review notification settings periodically ● Use device-level focus features when studying or working The objective is not to disconnect from communication. It is to make communication fit into daily life rather than constantly interrupting it. Telegram can remain useful without becoming the center of every moment. The broader educational lesson is valuable: technology should support daily goals, not replace them. The group contains classmates who share lecture notes, reminders, practice questions, and project information. The student begins by reviewing the group's purpose and communication rules. Instead of posting every question immediately, they search recent messages to see whether the topic has already been discussed. They also organize important documents and mute notifications during scheduled study sessions. This approach creates several learning outcomes. The student develops communication discipline, improves digital organization, and learns how to distinguish useful information from unnecessary conversation. The experience also demonstrates that Telegram can be more than a messaging tool. It can become a structured learning environment when users apply good organizational habits. Members use concise messages and establish expectations around response times. The team also encourages employees to review account settings and use appropriate authentication features. These habits make digital collaboration more organized. The main educational outcome is improved workplace communication. Team members learn how to communicate clearly, manage digital information, and respect other people's time. Good communication habits can make such a group more useful. Family members can avoid forwarding unnecessary information, respect personal boundaries, and use direct messages for conversations that are not relevant to everyone. This example shows how account and communication knowledge can support relationships. Digital tools work best when users understand both the technology and the social responsibilities associated with it. Case Study 4: A Hobby Community A hobby community may use Telegram to discuss photography, programming, fitness activities, language learning, cooking, or another shared interest. Members benefit when discussions remain organized and respectful. New participants can read community rules, introduce themselves appropriately, and learn from experienced members. The educational value extends beyond the hobby itself. Participants develop collaboration, information evaluation, communication, and community-participation skills. Step-by-Step Guide to Using a Telegram Account Safely Step 1: Review Your Account Profile Begin by opening your Telegram profile and reviewing the information currently displayed. Look at your username, profile photo, biography, and other visible information. Consider whether each item is appropriate for the people who may interact with your account. Remove information that is unnecessary or outdated. Step 2: Review Privacy Settings Open Telegram's privacy-related settings and examine each available category. Review options concerning: ● Phone number ● Last seen and online status ● Profile photos ● Calls ● Groups and channels ● Forwarded messages ● Other available interaction controls Choose settings based on your communication needs rather than copying another person's configuration. Step 3: Enable Additional Account Verification Review Telegram's two-step verification feature and determine whether you want to use it. If you enable it, create a strong, unique password that you can manage responsibly. Review recovery information and make sure you understand how account recovery works. Step 4: Review Active Sessions Periodically check the devices and sessions connected to your Telegram account. If you recognize all of the devices, you have a clearer picture of where the account is being used. If an old device is no longer needed, follow Telegram's available procedure for ending that session. This is a useful habit whenever you replace a phone, stop using a computer, or change devices. Step 5: Organize Groups and Channels Review the groups and channels you currently follow. Ask yourself: ● Is this community still useful? ● Do I need its notifications? ● Does the content support my goals? ● Is the group relevant to my work, study, family, or interests? Mute, archive, leave, or reorganize conversations when appropriate. Step 6: Practice Careful Information Sharing Before sending a file, photograph, link, or personal message, confirm the recipient and context. Take an extra moment with information that contains private details. This simple pause can become one of the most valuable digital habits you develop. Step 7: Establish a Monthly Review Once a month, spend a few minutes reviewing your Telegram account. Check privacy settings, active sessions, groups, channels, notifications, and profile information. Regular reviews are easier than trying to reorganize everything after a long period of use. Educational Benefits of Learning Telegram Account Management Improved Digital Literacy Understanding Telegram teaches users how modern communication platforms operate. Concepts such as authentication, privacy controls, sessions, notifications, and information sharing appear across many online services. Better Decision-Making Users learn to pause and evaluate information before acting. This applies to messages, links, files, group invitations, and account requests. Stronger Communication Skills Telegram communities provide opportunities to practice concise writing, respectful discussion, collaboration, and digital etiquette. Better Time Management Notification controls and organized conversations help users protect study time, work time, and personal time. Greater Independence When people understand account settings themselves, they become less dependent on others for routine digital tasks. Practical Career Skills Many workplaces use digital collaboration tools. Learning how to communicate clearly, manage shared information, and maintain professional online habits can support future employment and teamwork. Everyday Life Skills You Can Learn From Telegram Information Organization Managing conversations, files, groups, and channels encourages users to develop organizational systems. Personal Boundaries Managing notifications and availability can teach people to establish healthy boundaries around communication. Responsible Technology Use The broader lesson is balance. item.title: Why Touch Coordinates Do Not Match the Sensor Grid
item.content:encoded:
A touch controller reports an X position of 3072, but the display is only 800 pixels wide. Is the driver returning invalid data?

Not necessarily. A controller's coordinate range can differ from the display's pixel dimensions. It can also be much finer than the electrode matrix that produced the measurement.

For an embedded UI developer, these are three separate spaces: the physical sensor, the reported coordinates, and the rendered screen. Understanding the boundaries between them makes position errors easier to investigate.

The electrodes do not form a pixel address map

Touchscreen Channels are the transmit and receive channels used by the controller to measure the sensor. In a mutual-capacitance panel, the controller measures coupling between TX and RX electrodes. A finger changes that coupling near the contact area.

The resulting measurements support a position estimate. There is no requirement for one electrode intersection per LCD pixel.

As a hypothetical example, a full 16 TX × 28 RX matrix contains 448 sensing intersections. That number does not specify the coordinate range available to software. It also does not specify how many simultaneous fingers the controller can report.

This matters when reading a specification: a larger coordinate range is not proof of greater physical accuracy. A device can report many numerical positions while its measurements still contain noise or systematic error.

Convert the reported range, not the channel count

Suppose a hypothetical controller reports both axes from 0 through 4095. The application renders onto an 800 × 480 pixel surface.

For a simple mapping with aligned axes, no rotation, and the full sensor area covering the full display, the calculation is:

screen_x = round(raw_x * 799 / 4095)
        screen_y = round(raw_y * 479 / 4095)

The display's last pixel indices are 799 and 479. Using 800 and 480 as the output endpoints would allow coordinates outside that pixel index range.

Here, raw_x means a controller-reported coordinate before this mapping, not a raw capacitance measurement.

A reported position of approximately (2048, 2048) maps near the display center. The electrode count does not appear in the calculation.

If the input range has a nonzero minimum, subtract it before scaling:

screen_x = round((raw_x - x_min) * (width - 1) / (x_max - x_min))

This assumes x_max > x_min, valid input, and arithmetic with enough precision. In production code, define how to handle out-of-range values and avoid accidental integer truncation.

Before implementing any conversion, check whether the driver, compositor, or UI framework already performs it. Applying the same scaling twice creates another position error.

Rotation introduces a different problem

Scaling adjusts the range. Rotation changes which direction each axis represents.

For example, a finger moving horizontally across the mounted screen might primarily change the reported Y coordinate. That observation suggests an axis swap somewhere in the mapping. If the relevant coordinate decreases in the direction the application expects it to increase, an inversion may also be needed.

Linux's common touchscreen bindings define properties for axis inversion and swapping. They also define touchscreen-size-x and touchscreen-size-y in terms of the maximum reported coordinate plus one.

Those properties are not TX/RX electrode counts. Check support in the specific driver before changing them, and track transformations applied elsewhere in the software stack.

Use five locations to expose mapping errors

A quick check can start with the center and four locations near the corners. Use visible targets slightly inside the active area rather than assuming a finger can reach the exact numerical endpoint.

For each target, record the reported coordinate before application mapping and the final UI position.

Look for patterns:

  • A left-right reversal suggests an orientation problem.
  • A correct center with increasing displacement toward the edges suggests a range or scale mismatch.
  • Correct positions before UI mapping, followed by incorrect positions afterward, focus the investigation on that transformation.
  • Missing or unstable contacts before mapping require investigation beyond a coordinate formula.

These observations narrow the search; they do not establish a root cause by themselves. Five targets are a useful initial check, not a complete accuracy assessment.

Keep contact tracking out of the coordinate calculation

  • Config 파일: 마이크로소프트 인증 번호(OTP)를 낚아채기 위한 IMAP 서버 정보와 연동 도메인이 올바르게 입력되어 있어야 합니다.
  • Proxy 파일: 프록시 IP 목록(ip:port:user:pass)이 입력되어 있어야 합니다.
  • Task.csv 파일: Email 및 Password 열에 대상 계정 정보가 입력되어 있어야 합니다.
  • Ron’s CSV Editor: CSV 데이터의 열이 밀리는 것을 방지하기 위해 권장되는 전용 편집기입니다.

프록시 관련 주의사항: 봇이 에러 메시지 없이 갑자기 중단되는 경우 프록시 연결을 가장 먼저 확인하세요. 응답하지 않는 IP는 기능의 자동 정지를 유발합니다.

권장 작업 실행 순서

🔍 Check Emails → 📧 Set Recovery → 🔐 Set 2FA → 🔄 Change Password → 📨 Set Rule

중요: 각 단계는 이전 단계의 완료 상태에 엄격하게 의존합니다. 이 순서를 준수해야 마이크로소프트 보안 알고리즘을 자극하지 않고 계정 정지(잠김)를 방지할 수 있습니다.

1단계: 계정 보안 상태 확인 (Check Emails)

Check for Security 옵션을 활성화한 상태에서 Check Emails 기능을 실행합니다.

  • 성공 (Successful): 계정에 사전 보안 설정이 없으며, 자동화 작업을 진행할 준비가 된 상태입니다.
  • 제외 대상 (Worth protection): 계정에 이미 제3자의 복구 수단이 등록되어 있습니다. 복구 권한이 없다면 작업이 불가능하므로 작업 목록(Task.csv)에서 제외하세요.

2단계: 복구 이메일 연동 (Set Recovery Email)

Set Recovery Email 기능을 실행합니다. Settings 탭에서 연동할 복구 이메일 방식을 선택합니다.

  • 성공 (Successful): RecoveryEmail 열에 본인 도메인의 복구 주소가 등록됩니다.
  • 주요 오류 (Limit send OTP 또는 IMAP failed): Config 파일에 설정된 IMAP 연결이 마이크로소프트에서 보낸 인증 메일을 정상적으로 수신하지 못함을 의미합니다.

3단계: 2단계 인증 활성화 (Set 2FA)

Set 2FA 기능을 실행합니다. 봇이 표준 TOTP 비밀키(Google Authenticator 호환)를 자동으로 생성합니다.

  • 성공 (Successful): 2FA 열에 생성된 시크릿 키가 저장됩니다 (예: JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP).
  • 실패 원인: 2단계를 건너뛴 경우 발생합니다. 2FA는 유효한 복구 이메일이 반드시 사전에 등록되어 있어야 활성화됩니다.

팁: 생성된 2FA 키가 포함된 CSV 파일의 백업본을 안전한 장소에 별도로 보관하세요.

4단계: 비밀번호 일괄 변경 (Change Passwords)

Change Security 메뉴에서 Change Password 옵션을 활성화하고 실행합니다.

  • 성공 (Successful): Password 열에 새로 생성된 무작위 비밀번호가 업데이트됩니다.
  • 실패 원인: 사전에 2FA 또는 복구 이메일이 설정되지 않은 계정은 변경 작업이 차단됩니다.

5단계: 메일 리디렉션 규칙 설정 (Set Rule)

  1. Task.csv 파일을 열고 Forward/Redirect 열에 모든 메일을 받아볼 마스터 수신함 주소를 입력합니다.
  2. Settings 메뉴에서 필요한 옵션(Redirect to, Remove old rule, Disable App Forwarding)을 설정한 뒤 Set Rule을 실행합니다.
  • 성공 (Successful): 이 계정들로 들어오는 모든 수신 메일이 마스터 수신함으로 자동 리디렉션됩니다.

핵심 원칙: 리디렉션 설정이 완료된 후에는 해당 계정에 웹 브라우저로 직접 로그인하지 마세요. 인터랙티브 웹 로그인은 마이크로소프트 보안 검사를 트리거하여 설정된 전송 규칙을 초기화(취소)시킬 수 있습니다.

작업 순서가 왜 필수적인가요?

  • 2FA 활성화를 위해서는 사전에 유효한 복구 이메일이 반드시 등록되어 있어야 합니다.
  • 서버 전송 규칙(Set Rule) 등록은 2FA와 복구 이메일이 모두 준비된 상태에서만 안전하게 실행됩니다.
  • 단계를 건너뛰면 계정 챌린지 및 보안 락이 발생하여 자동화가 중단됩니다.
